initial_events.summary: Late-2025 expectations include active discussion of a possible quarter-point cut, but no pre-commitment.
initial_events.expected_impact: Keeps cut and hold both live; raises attention without resolving committee balance.

initial_events.summary: Recent communication stresses data dependence over forward commitment.
initial_events.expected_impact: Suppresses overconfidence in any single endpoint and raises importance of incoming data signals.

initial_events.summary: Additional inflation and labor indicators arrive before the meeting and can shift internal coalition weights.
initial_events.expected_impact: Potential repricing of cut odds and faction influence depending on data direction.

initial_events.summary: Committee issues the December 10, 2025 statement establishing whether the target range is lower than before the meeting.
initial_events.expected_impact: Terminal endpoint evidence becomes available; implementation-only changes should not alter resolution.

meta.important_question: Will the FOMC lower the target range for the federal funds rate at the December 10, 2025 meeting relative to immediately before the meeting?

endpoint_ledger.label: Target range lowered at December 10 meeting
endpoint_ledger.rationale: Markets discuss a possible quarter-point cut, and labor softening could justify easing if persuasive enough.
endpoint_ledger.description: The federal funds target range is lower immediately after the December 10, 2025 statement than immediately before the meeting.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Possible but not pre-committed; mixed signals keep path open.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Any implementation-detail adjustment without lower target range fails realization.

meta.important_question: By the eve of the meeting, do incoming data appear to shift the effective internal balance toward hawks, doves, or leave centrists dominant?

endpoint_ledger.label: Target range unchanged at December 10 meeting
endpoint_ledger.rationale: Inflation still above target and absence of pre-commitment support a hold as a credible baseline.
endpoint_ledger.description: The federal funds target range is not lower immediately after the December 10, 2025 statement than immediately before the meeting.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Slightly favored because communication is data-dependent and inflation remains above target.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A dovish statement tone alone does not negate this endpoint if the range is unchanged.

meta.important_question: Before the meeting, does market and analyst consensus move toward treating a 25bp cut as the base case or remain split/lean hold?

endpoint_ledger.label: Internal coalition shifts toward easing before vote
endpoint_ledger.rationale: The decisive swing actor set is likely the centrist bloc rather than fixed hawk/dove camps.
endpoint_ledger.description: Observable pre-meeting evidence indicates centrists move closer to the dovish case for a cut.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Not yet realized; mixed signals leave coalition movement unresolved.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This can realize without the final cut endpoint if late caution or consensus constraints intervene.

meta.important_question: At decision time, is there any technical or implementation change that creates headline confusion without satisfying the target-range-lowered criterion?

endpoint_ledger.label: Technical change without target-range cut
endpoint_ledger.rationale: The source packet specifically warns not to misread implementation details as endpoint realization.
endpoint_ledger.description: A procedural or implementation-detail change occurs that does not lower the target range and therefore does not satisfy the yes endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Explicitly flagged as a possible source of confusion by the corpus.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: If the target range is lowered, this endpoint may co-occur as a secondary mechanism but does not supersede yes.

simulation_brief.summary: Late-2025 FOMC decision environment with markets discussing a possible quarter-point cut amid mixed labor-market softening and inflation still above target. Policymakers emphasize data dependence rather than pre-commitment. Terminal question is whether the target range for the federal funds rate is lower immediately after the December 10, 2025 meeting statement than immediately before the meeting.
simulation_brief.resolution_rule: yes only if target range is lower immediately after the December 10, 2025 statement than immediately before the meeting; implementation-detail changes alone do not count.
simulation_brief.initial_state_uncertainty: High uncertainty around whether labor softening or inflation persistence dominates the committee decision. Source corpus is sparse and defines endpoint tightly.

branch_hypotheses.trigger: Pre-meeting labor data weakens materially while inflation progress does not reverse.
branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Centrists align with doves for a 25bp cut.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Analyst and market commentary shifts from optionality framing to base-case cut framing; committee communication tolerates easing interpretation.

branch_hypotheses.trigger: Inflation readings remain sticky enough to keep above-target concern salient.
branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Committee holds target range steady despite prior easing expectations.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Hawk commentary gains narrative dominance and market-implied cut odds fall meaningfully before the meeting.

branch_hypotheses.trigger: Implementation details or technical adjustments are discussed near meeting time.
branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Public confusion rises but endpoint remains no unless target range itself is lowered.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Media headlines emphasize change while careful analysts note unchanged target range.

branch_hypotheses.trigger: Mixed data persists without decisive deterioration or inflation relief.
branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Committee preserves optionality by holding rates while signaling openness to future easing.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Statement language softens or guidance tone shifts but target range remains unchanged.

sociology_baseline.note: Interpretations cluster around plausible cut-versus-hold ranges rather than extreme outcomes.
A few decisive data releases could shift internal coalition balance toward cut or hold.
Most households have preferences but low direct expression on central-bank implementation details.
Traders and analysts consume similar expert and media signals, reinforcing clustered narratives.
A cut narrative becomes more credible if repeated across data, analyst notes, and official remarks.
Institutional identity favors disciplined, credibility-preserving process over abrupt signaling shifts.
Outside major data releases and the meeting itself, broad public attention remains limited.
